genxml.title: VC3 video controller registers of the Impact graphics subsystem
genxml.doc: Video timing, hardware cursor and display-ID controller on the display bus. Its internal registers are numbered 0 to 31 and are reached through a small set of ports in the chip's display-bus window; the ports are the byte-addressed registers, the numbered registers are the vc3_index space (offset = register number). Each numbered register is 16 bits wide. The window address depends on the board's map and is not given here. Grades follow the repository legend; a bit named in a header and never seen used is inferred.

struct.name: INDEX
struct.doc: Port: selects the numbered register that the data port reads or writes (a one-byte access at the start of the window).

struct.name: INDEX_DATA
struct.doc: Port: a three-byte write sets a numbered register in one store, the register number in bits 31:24 and the 16-bit value in bits 23:8. The kernel and the diagnostic use it for every register write.

struct.name: DATA
struct.doc: Port: reads or writes the numbered register that the index port last selected, 16 bits at a time. The diagnostic reads a register back by writing its number to the index port and reading this port.

struct.name: RAM64
struct.doc: Port: SRAM access four bytes wide per bus transfer, written as a 64-bit store. The software defines it next to the 16-bit port and uses the same SRAM address register.

struct.name: RAM
struct.doc: Port: reads or writes the SRAM word addressed by ram_addr, 16 bits at a time (the kernel and the diagnostic load the timing tables, the cursor glyph and the display-ID tables through it).

struct.name: VID_EP
struct.doc: Video timing entry point, the main display frame table pointer. The diagnostic's register test writes walking patterns and expects them back unchanged.

struct.name: CURS_EP
struct.doc: Cursor entry point. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: CURS_X
struct.doc: Hardware cursor x position. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: CURS_Y
struct.doc: Hardware cursor y position. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: DID_EP1
struct.doc: First display-ID entry point, with its own frame and line tables.

struct.name: DID_EP2
struct.doc: Second display-ID entry point.

struct.name: SCAN_LENGTH
struct.doc: Scan line length. Walking-pattern read-back is expected; the unit (dot clocks) is the name's reading and is inferred.

struct.name: RAM_ADDR
struct.doc: SRAM address register for the ram port. Reads back the address it was loaded with.

struct.name: VT_FRAME_TBL_PTR
struct.doc: Video timing frame table pointer. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: VT_LINE_SEQ_PTR
struct.doc: Video timing line sequence pointer. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: VT_LINES_RUN
struct.doc: Video timing run count of lines. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: VERT_LINE_COUNT
struct.doc: Current vertical line. The kernel reads it (the only numbered register it reads); the diagnostic's register test also writes walking patterns here and expects them back, which is odd for a running counter and is recorded as the software's expectation.

struct.name: CURS_TBL_PTR
struct.doc: Cursor table pointer. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: WORKING_CURS_Y
struct.doc: Working cursor y line. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: CUR_CURSOR_X
struct.doc: Current cursor x. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: UNUSED
struct.doc: Register number the diagnostic's register test writes and reads back under the name unused. Its role is unknown.

struct.name: DID_FRAMETAB1
struct.doc: Frame table pointer of the first display-ID entry point. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: DID_LINETAB1
struct.doc: Line table pointer of the first display-ID entry point. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: DID_FRAMETAB2
struct.doc: Frame table pointer of the second display-ID entry point. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: DID_LINETAB2
struct.doc: Line table pointer of the second display-ID entry point. Walking-pattern read-back is expected.

struct.name: CURS_CONTROL
struct.doc: Cursor control. The standalone initialisation sets the function and display bits to turn the cursor on; the hosted build of the same routine writes the complement of that pair, with a comment that the X server turns the cursor on later. The diagnostic's start and stop timing write zero. The register test skips it.

struct.name: DISPLAY_CONTROL
struct.doc: Display control. The kernel keeps a shadow of the value, never reads the register back and writes it through the index_data port for retrace enable, blackout, timing and genlock; the diagnostic reads it back. The register test skips it. Every field is named in a header and read from the writers' use; what bits 1 to 4 and 7 do inside the chip is not settled.

struct.name: CONFIG
struct.doc: Master configuration. The diagnostic's PLL set-up writes 1 and prints that the register is set to 1; the kernel selects this register to read the chip revision at attach. Bits other than the revision are named in a header only.
